topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets the course context, and outlines the core learning objectives concerning cancer causation and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Intrinsic and Endogenous Drivers of Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the foundational nature of cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease driven by endogenous mutational processes, replication errors, and inherited genetic predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures, Epidemiological Evidence, and the Cancer Risk Debate
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the epidemiological and geographic evidence linking environmental exposures to cancer risk while exploring the debate surrounding intrinsic bad luck versus extrinsic causation.

topics.label: Biological and Chemical Mechanisms of Carcinogens and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the specific biological and molecular mechanisms by which diverse carcinogenic agents, metabolic processes, tumor promoters, and developmental susceptibilities drive neoplastic transformation.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Evaluating Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches utilized to establish mutational signatures and determine whether agents are carcinogenic.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with closing framing on everyday risk-benefit choices and key takeaways regarding environmental cancer causation.
